history.dynasty: None (modern; built by BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha)
history.summary: BAPS mandir on Kalavad Road, Rajkot, completed in 1998; the decision to build was taken in the 1990s as the satsang congregation grew, and the temple came up under the guidance of Yogiji Maharaj. Built by ancient Vedic Shilpa Shastra methods using Ambaji marble, Makrana marble and Udaipur pink marble, with pink stone from Bansipahadpur, Rajasthan (the same stone used at Akshardham, Gandhinagar). Its three sanctums house a Panchdhatu (five-metal) murti of Harikrishna Maharaj, marble icons of Radha-Krishna, Bhagwan Swaminarayan, Gunatitanand Swami, Gopalanand Swami and Ghanshyam Maharaj, along with murtis of the guru parampara (Bhagatji Maharaj, Shastriji Maharaj, Yogiji Maharaj, Pramukh Swami Maharaj). The mandir is also known for its charitable trust and humanitarian work, and enforces a modest dress code for visitors.

name: BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, Rajkot
town_description: Rajkot is the fourth-largest city of Gujarat and a major commercial, industrial and educational hub of the Saurashtra region. Once the capital of the princely state of Rajkot and an administrative centre of the Saurashtra region, it is also the city where Mahatma Gandhi spent his early years. The city is well connected by air (Rajkot International Airport at Hirasar), rail (Rajkot Junction) and road (NH-27).

travel.airport: Rajkot Civil Airport ~5.1 km; Rajkot International Airport (Hirasar) further out (verify).
travel.road: Central bus stand ~3.2 km (verify); well connected by state and private buses to major Gujarat cities.
